text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Eight villagers killed in Medea, south of Algiers.

- Abdallah Djaballah, leader of Islamist-oriented Nahda party, said in a campaign rally in the eastern town of Guelma the "country's rulers are from eastern Algeria but the eastern areas are underdeveloped".

- Hocine Ait Ahmed, head of the secular opposition Socialist Forces Front (FFS), said Algeria's main legal Islamist-leaning Movement for a Peaceful Society "is more dangerous than the outlawed radical Islamic Salvation Front (FIS)".
- Algeria ended a third round of talks with the Euroepan Union on an trade association accord.
- President Liamine Zeroual meets poll watching body officials.
- Pro-government National Democratic Rally party to sue Islamist Nahda over a ballot paper leakage.
- Ait Ahmed said the June 5 elections would be "surrealistic" because people are hostages of the "Islamist and state terrors".
